messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: spike detected - POST /v1/uploads (app-uploads) from 198.51.100.0/24 and several ASNs. 5xx rate 12.3% over last 5m, p95 latency 1.8s. auto-page oncall.

emma: paging @oncall-eu — can you take?

oncall-eu: on it, joining.

raj: I'm seeing repeated multipart uploads with tiny payloads, about 10k req/sec from ~200 IPs. Looks like scraper/probe farm. Headers show sequential user-agents like "okhttp" and blank referrers.

maria: impact: uploads endpoint 503s for a subset of customers on dedicated pools; batch ingestion queues backing up. Customer-facing error rate up ~3% for customers using /uploads/batch.

oncall-eu: first mitigation: enable tiered rate limit for /v1/uploads for anonymous / non-authed tokens to 5 r/s per IP and apply stricter quota for new tokens. rolling apply to edge for 5 regions.

sre-rotation: applying edge rate-limit rule now:
```
POST /api/edge/rate-limits
{
  "path": "/v1/uploads",
  "match": {"auth_type":"none"},
  "limit": "5r/s",
  "burst": 10
}
```

oncall-eu: pushing WAF rule to block known scraping UA patterns and IP ranges behaving like proxies. Adding captcha challenge for POSTs that exceed 10/min per token.

security: adding fingerprint block for identical session cookies + rapid token churn. Also enabling geo-fence for region with most traffic (SG/APAC) to soft-block.

emma: note — need to alert affected customers. @customer-success can you draft a short notice: we've throttled uploads due to abusive traffic; some customers on dedicated pools may see transient 503s.

customer-success: drafting. Will send to accounts flagged in alerts and publish a status page update (minor degradation).

raj: small test before wide rollout: curl simulation
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/uploads -d @tiny.json &
done
```
Got 429s after rule applied. Good.

maria: batching ingestion backlog decreased after the edge limits. CPU on batch workers down from 92% to 45% in 6 minutes. Errors trending down.

oncall-eu: enabled circuit breaker: if errors > 5% for 3m, redirect heavy clients to read-only mode and reject new uploads for that API key class.

sre-rotation: noting we've temporarily disabled /v1/uploads/batch for unauthenticated traffic. Leaving for 30m and will reassess.

security: WAF blocks currently affecting ~0.6% of total IPs but matching 95% of abusive requests. No known false positives yet.

emma: customer impact: 12 customers in ticketing reported increased 503s, two customers on dedicated pools impacted more severely. CS contacting them directly.

customer-success: message sent to affected accounts, included mitigation steps and ETA 30-60m for stability. Posted to status.redwood.ai (minor incident).

oncall-eu: handing off to @sre-rotation for next shift. leaving notes in incident board: actions taken, rules IDs, customers notified, rollback plan.

sre-rotation: taking over. continue monitoring logs+ dashboards. recommend follow-up postmortem to review quota settings and bot-detection signatures.

emma: good job team. keep the thread updated with any regression. I'll open an incident ticket #INC-2026-147 and assign to security+infra for full analysis.

incident-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-147 (uploads-abuse). Pager duty -> oncall-eu acknowledged. :white_check_mark:

maria: leaving retention note: capture 1h of raw access logs for the 198.51.100.0/24 range and store in /incidents/INC-2026-147/artifacts.

sre-rotation: monitoring: last 10m 5xx down to 1.1%, p95 latency 480ms. Keeping soft WAF and rate-limits for additional 45m.

security: will schedule a rule tuning session tomorrow. consider adaptive rate-limiting per token entropy and UA heuristics.

oncall-eu: closing handoff. ping me if anything heats up. :thumbsup:

sre-rotation: acknowledge, will escalate if >2% errors reappear.

customer-success: final note to customers will include: apology, what we did, expected time to full recovery, and a link to postmortem once ready.

emma: closing thread shortly once metrics stable for 1h. Thanks all. :eyes:
